title: Enhancing the Well-Being of Hospitalized Patients Through XR Technology
summary:
The Center for Virtual and Extended Reality in Medicine (ZvRM) at University Medicine Essen is investigating whether the use of Extended Reality (XR) can improve the wellbeing of hospitalized patients. XR enables patients to briefly “step out” of their hospital environment through virtual experiences – for example, by visiting relaxing nature scenes, playing games, or sharing activities with friends and family.

Many people experience negative feelings such as anxiety, stress, pain, or boredom during a hospital stay. XR applications are intended to help reduce these burdens and enhance positive feelings such as relaxation, joy, and a sense of self-efficacy.

Within the project, specially trained nurses – called “XR Advanced Nurses” – are deployed. They select suitable XR content, accompany patients during use, and document the outcomes.

The effects of XR are being investigated in a study that assesses patients’ psychological wellbeing (e.g., mood, anxiety, pain, relaxation) as well as their satisfaction with the XR service.
conditions: Well-being and patient experience during inpatient stays at University Hospital Essen through the use of XR technology

interventions.name: One-time, guided XR intervention in the patient's room lasting 10-30 minutes

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Data triangulation will be used to include patients from different clinical departments and with varying demographic and medical backgrounds (e.g., age, disease, phase of treatment) in the study.

Only patients who are able to give their consent and use XR headsets safely can participate in the study.

Sufficient knowledge of German is essential for answering the questionnaires and accompanying materials in order to avoid misunderstandings. Non-German speakers are therefore not eligible to participate in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
People with certain neurological conditions are not eligible to participate, such as:
•    photosensitive epilepsy
•    dementia
•    delirium or transient syndrome
•    severe mental illness such as schizophrenia
•    severe susceptibility to nausea (motion sickness) 
•    balance disorders

In accordance with the safety instructions provided in the user manual for standard XR headsets, individuals who wear or have implanted the following medical devices are excluded from participating in the study:
•    Pacemakers
•    Implantable defibrillators
•    Hearing aids
